name: Subbasta
description: Aggregator for Malta's judicial property auctions. It presents court-sale data in a usable way and translates official documents from Maltese. Subscription for platform access, plus Power-of-Attorney onboarding €249, property viewing €150/property, legal research from €199, and a 1% success fee on winning bids. Founded Dec 2025, Malta.

mentions.evidence: ~$3,606 MRR, 126 active subscriptions, ~$5,079 L30, ~$58,575 all-time, ~80% L30 profit margin, L30 MRR growth −12.1%. Revenue synced Oct 6, 2026 ~05:44 Warsaw (03:44 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Do the same for PL komornicze licytacje (court-bailiff auctions on licytacje.komornik.pl / e-licytacje), or for CZ/SK dražby. Alerts by city/price + document summaries + paid "we'll inspect / handle paperwork" add-ons.

whyItPrints: Public court notices sitting in a clunky government format. Investors pay to see them first and in English. In under a year it has 126 subs, and the service add-ons + success fee turn a data feed into a transaction business.
whyThisMatters:
People following Malta's court property sales get the list in English. Subbasta pulls the auctions from the eCourts site and translates the official papers from Maltese. You can read a file before the sale, and their lawyer can bid for you on the day.

The subscription is the platform. A one-time power of attorney lets that lawyer bid, and later bids through them carry no separate per-bid fee. An exterior look is free to arrange. An interior viewing means the lawyer files the court application. Legal research runs from a short summary up to a signed opinion. If they place the winning bid, the listing adds a one percent fee.

The company started in Malta in December 2025.
